propositions: A committed uv.lock freezes transitive dependencies, causing any published advisory on a pinned version to block all in-flight changes via a gating pip-audit job, punishing authors who did not cause or cannot fix the advisory.

The Gerrit verify gate now blocks on an outstanding CRITICAL/HIGH advisory only when the change touches the dependency map (uv.lock, pyproject.toml, requirements files), exempting unrelated changes from false failures.

A daily scheduled canary runs pip-audit against main and escalates outstanding advisories via automated ticket filing with dedup, ensuring CRITICAL/HIGH findings are visible to lock owners rather than silently blocking releases.

override-dependencies is the correct instrument to patch a vulnerable cap when upgrading the direct dependency is blocked by an upstream constraint; constraint-dependencies can only NARROW and returns UNSATISFIABLE as its expected output, not as proof of impossibility.

The runbook documents severity tiers (CRITICAL/HIGH fail, MEDIUM warns, LOW tracked), the recovery path (upgrade direct dependency → override with justification → track upstream fix), and the verification set (uv lock --check, uv sync --locked --extra dev, full pip-audit).
Release authorization is gated by the same advisory check, preventing shipping on a known-vulnerable pin while allowing dependency-map-touching changes to own and resolve their own findings.
